name: Healthcare Providers
one_liner: Hospitals, health systems and physician groups deliver care with high fixed costs and labor intensity, while their prices are set largely by government and negotiated insurer rates.
how_it_makes_money: Providers bill for services delivered, under fee-for-service, per-case (DRG) or, increasingly, value-based and capitated arrangements. Revenue depends heavily on payer mix: commercial insurers pay well above Medicare, which in turn pays more than Medicaid.
revenue_formula: Revenue = patient volume (admissions, visits, procedures) × acuity/case mix × net reimbursement rate
Net reimbursement = Σ payer mix share × payer rate - denials and bad debt
Capitated revenue = attributed members × per-member-per-month payment
cost_structure: Labor: nurses, physicians and staff, often roughly half or more of hospital operating costs
Supplies and drugs: implants, pharmaceuticals, medical supplies
Facilities and equipment: buildings, imaging and surgical capital
Administration and revenue cycle: billing, coding, IT and EHR
Purchased services and contract labor: agency staffing, outsourced functions
margins: Nonprofit health systems often run thin operating margins in the low single digits, while some for-profit chains and specialized outpatient operators do better; payer mix, labor costs and site of care drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Operating margin
key_metrics.what: Operating income over revenue; the headline measure of financial health for health systems.

key_metrics.name: Payer mix
key_metrics.what: Share of revenue by commercial, Medicare, Medicaid and self-pay; a primary driver of profitability.

key_metrics.name: Case mix index (CMI)
key_metrics.what: Average acuity of inpatients; higher acuity means higher reimbursement per case.

key_metrics.name: Average length of stay (ALOS)
key_metrics.what: Days per inpatient admission; shorter stays free capacity and cut cost per case.

key_metrics.name: Bed occupancy rate
key_metrics.what: Share of staffed beds in use; shows capacity utilization.

key_metrics.name: Days in accounts receivable (A/R days)
key_metrics.what: Time to collect payment; measures revenue cycle efficiency.

key_metrics.name: Labor cost per adjusted discharge
key_metrics.what: Labor spend normalized for volume; tracks workforce productivity.

trends: Nursing and clinician shortages keeping labor costs elevated
Care shifting from inpatient hospitals to outpatient, ambulatory surgery and home settings
Gradual move toward value-based care and risk-bearing contracts
Health system mergers and physician practice acquisitions under antitrust scrutiny
Pressure on Medicaid funding and coverage affecting safety-net providers
AI for clinical documentation, scheduling and revenue cycle

case_angles.question: A hospital system's margins have turned negative. How do you restore profitability?
Should a health system build an ambulatory surgery center network?
Emergency department wait times are rising. How should the hospital improve patient flow?
Should two neighboring health systems merge?

interview_hooks: Does hospital consolidation improve care or mostly raise prices?
Will value-based care ever overtake fee-for-service?
Should site-neutral payment equalize what hospitals and clinics are paid for the same service?
